item.title: Darmanin says Mélenchon or Le Pen would destroy the European Community
item.description: The French justice minister backed Edouard Philippe as the pro-European candidate for the 2027 election, calling at a Barcelona forum for Europe to rearm and become a power rather than a place of discussion.

item.title: Parliament to debate EU cybersecurity plan for hospitals, schools and power grids
item.description: The debate on 11 November follows a January Commission proposal to tighten the union's ICT supply chains and give ENISA a stronger role. No step in the procedure has yet been recorded.

item.title: EU picks Proximus and three other suppliers for six-year sovereign cloud contract
item.description: The Belgian state still owns 53% of Proximus. The framework deal covers the Commission, Parliament, Council and 70 agencies.

item.title: Brussels found the addiction. Now it must ban the design, not the bans.
item.description: The Commission's own findings name the machinery of Meta's and TikTok's addictive design, yet after two years and five sets of findings there is no final decision and no scroll switched off. With lawmakers in seven countries moving to ban infinite scroll, autoplay and luring notifications, the Commission should write the ban Europe-wide into the Digital Fairness Act instead of calling the patchwork fragmentation.
